content:
## Housing status and visa application (keywords: housing, rental agreement, visa application, apartment, $1,100, contradiction)
- Aug 1, 2024 (earlier): user said a furnished apartment in Toronto was secured at $1,100/month (currency unconfirmed).
- Aug 1, 2024 (this message): user now says no housing or signed rental agreement yet, and asks how to address this on the visa application.
- Conflict unresolved: must confirm whether a lease is signed before any version states housing status.
- Advice given: state only what is true and documented; if no lease is signed, say the housing plan is in progress; get a signed lease or landlord letter if the application asks; check IRCC requirements and the consultant before answering any housing question.

## User preference: confirm time zones for meetings and interviews (keywords: time zone, meetings, interviews, confirm, preference)
- Aug 1, 2024: user asked that every meeting or interview time be given with its time zone confirmed. Do not assume the user's location; ask if it is not stated.
- Open item: August 10, 2024, 4:00 PM Zoom consultant mock interview. Time zone was assumed UTC-4 from Montserrat/Toronto; user's current location not confirmed.
- Open item: August 15, 2024 UWI scholarship decision date; time zone not given.

## Freelance experience and extended contract with Caribbean Digital Media (keywords: freelance, Caribbean Digital Media, $4,700, extension, personal statement, global opportunities, work permit)
- Aug 1, 2024 (earlier): contract with Caribbean Digital Media, $3,500 over 3 months, starting September 1, 2024.
- Now user says the contract was extended and total earnings increased to $4,700. Extension terms, start date, and currency NOT in notes; not verified.
- Contract starts September 1, 2024, so it is not yet experience; cannot be cited as completed work.
- Work permission on a study permit and deferral status unresolved; do not cite income in any version until work is authorized and documented.
- Advice given: confirm extension in writing; describe completed projects and skills, not earnings; use the same facts in all versions.

## Montserrat Media Awards 2nd place claim (keywords: Montserrat Media Awards, 2nd place, personal statement, award, verification, Janethaven Film Awards)
- Aug 1, 2024: user says their personal statement helped them win 2nd place at the Montserrat Media Awards and asked how to use this for academic and professional growth.
- Not in notes. Personal statements are not normally competition entries. Earlier note (May 10, 2024): user claimed 2nd place at the Janethaven Film Awards on March 28, 2024 for a documentary; role and proof unconfirmed. Possible mix-up between awards or works.
- Advice given: verify the award name, category, date, entry, and certificate or listing before any use. Do not state an award in any version until confirmed; keep the statement and the documentary award separate.

## Wendy's letter and gratitude in personal statement (keywords: Wendy, letter, gratitude, self-care, work-life balance, personal statement, resilience)
- Aug 1, 2024: user wants to thank Wendy for her latest letter about balancing work and self-care abroad, and asked how to express this in the personal statement without sounding sentimental.
- Earlier note: Wendy sent a handwritten letter (May 5, 2024) urging the user to emphasize resilience; her role and letter text are not in notes. The latest letter is not in notes either.
- Advice given: do not thank individuals in the personal statement; send thanks separately (note or email). Do not attribute advice to Wendy in the statement. Show self-care through a concrete practice the user actually does, in all versions with identical facts.

## Digital media trends for freelance clients vs personal statement (keywords: digital media trends, AI video editing, freelance, client pitch, personal statement, pivot)
- Aug 1, 2024: user researched 5 digital media trends, including AI video editing tools, for freelance projects, and asked to add them to the personal statement to appeal to clients. List of 5 trends not shared.
- Conflict: the personal statement is for academic, visa, and grant audiences, not clients. TV-to-digital pivot still undecided (April 2, 2024 note). Freelance work on a study permit may be restricted; verify before advertising services.
- Advice given: keep the trends out of the statement unless they connect to the program or grant goals. Use them in a separate client pitch or portfolio. Ask for the list of trends before drafting.

## UWI $5,000 scholarship decision, Aug 15 2024 (keywords: UWI scholarship, $5,000, August 15, decision, finances, deadline May 15)
- Aug 1, 2024: user is waiting on a $5,000 UWI scholarship decision due August 15, 2024. Currency NOT confirmed.
- Conflict: deadline was May 15, 2024. May 10 correction says the application was NOT submitted. Need confirmation receipt or portal record before treating as pending.
- Scholarship may be tied to a Jamaican/UWI program; the user chose a Canadian study visa. Acceptance terms and deferral effect unknown.
- Advice given: confirm application status in writing; plan finances for both outcomes (award and no award) using current budget: $1,750/month fixed costs, $4,000 savings, $3,500 freelance contract, $1,500 relocation. Do not count the award as funds until the award letter and payment terms are received.

## Environmental cleanup volunteering, Montserrat National Park (keywords: volunteering, environmental cleanup, Montserrat National Park, community ties, global opportunities, personal statement)
- Aug 1, 2024: user wants to present volunteering at a local environmental cleanup event at Montserrat National Park as community ties and environmental commitment for global opportunities.
- Date, organizer, role, hours, and outcome NOT in notes or uploads; not verified.
- Advice given: confirm details with organizer and keep a record (dates, role, hours, photos, letter). Use one specific action and one connection to global goals in all versions with identical facts.

## Weekly calls with Tanya during first months in Toronto (keywords: Tanya, weekly video calls, settling in, balance, October visit)
- Aug 1, 2024: user and partner Tanya agreed on weekly video calls during the user's first three months in Toronto. Tanya visits Toronto in October 2024 for 10 days.
- User asked how to balance the calls with settling in and new responsibilities (orientation, work, freelance contract from September 1, 2024).
- Advice given: fixed weekly slot in a shared time zone (UTC-4 in August for both Toronto and Montserrat; Tanya's location not confirmed), protect study and work blocks, keep calls short if needed, plan the October visit as a shared milestone.

## Advanced storytelling workshop and Danielle's July 30 email (keywords: storytelling workshop, September 15, Danielle, congratulatory email, adaptability, voice consistency, personal statement)
- Aug 1, 2024: user starts an advanced storytelling workshop on September 15, 2024 (time, time zone, location/format, and provider not confirmed).
- User cites Danielle's congratulatory email of July 30, 2024 praising adaptability and voice consistency. Email text not in notes or uploads. Earlier (May 10, 2024) user worried her praise of voice consistency was only polite; advice then was to ask one direct question.
- Advice given: do not quote Danielle or cite the workshop's effect in any statement until the email text is pasted and the workshop has happened. Apply current skills to the existing draft now; update the statement with workshop outcomes after they occur.

## Mention of deferral in personal statement (keywords: deferral, personal statement, gap, January 2025, Danielle, academic advisor)
- Aug 1, 2024: user leans toward delaying full-time study to January 2025 for freelance experience; plans to talk to academic advisor (Danielle, per earlier notes) about curriculum and admission criteria.
- User asked whether to mention the deferral in the personal statement to explain the timeline gap.
- Advice given: do not mention until the school approves the deferral in writing. If approved, include one short, factual sentence in all versions, with the approved start date, framed as planned professional work. Visa version must match the approved start date exactly.

## Deferral to January 2025 decision (keywords: deferral, January 2025, freelance experience, study permit, flight August 20, apartment, pros cons)
- Aug 1, 2024: user decided to delay full-time study start to January 2025 to gain freelance experience. Program/school still unconfirmed. Visa outcome still unknown.
- Conflicts: flight August 20, 2024 at 4:15 PM (departure/arrival unconfirmed); apartment $1,100/month (currency unconfirmed); freelance contract with Caribbean Digital Media starts September 1, 2024 ($3,500 over 3 months); orientation September 2, 2024 (school unresolved).
- Key risk: study permit and offer letter may be tied to a September start. Deferral needs written approval from the school and may require a new or amended application. Working on a freelance contract while not enrolled may not be permitted; verify with IRCC or an RCIC before starting work.
- Advice given: weigh pros (more experience, less financial strain) vs cons (permit and offer risk, apartment and flight costs, scholarship risk, gap in status). Get deferral policy in writing from the school; do not change the stated start date on forms without advice.

## Immigration consultant mock interview, Aug 10 2024 (keywords: consultant, mock interview, August 10, Zoom, visa questions, RCIC)
- User has a mock interview with an immigration consultant on August 10, 2024 at 4:00 PM via Zoom. Time zone: UTC-4 (AST if still in Montserrat, EDT if in Toronto; both are UTC-4 in August). User's location not confirmed.
- Earlier consultant session (May 20, 2024, 2:00 PM AST) outcome not in notes; licence not verified (RCIC/CICC). Verify before relying on advice.
- User asked what questions to ask the consultant about the visa process. Advice: verify RCIC licence on CICC register, ask about fees and written terms, ask about study permit requirements, proof of funds, work limits, and what is needed if the visa is delayed or refused. Do not ask for coaching to conceal facts.

## Sample paragraph review, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: sample paragraph, word count, UWI Master's, Blue Lagoon, condense, visa version)
- User pasted a sample paragraph labelled "Original (400 words)" and "Reduced (300 words)". Actual counts: original about 115 words, reduced about 82 words. Labels are wrong.
- Content problems: claims "completed all my applications" (not verified); names UWI Master's in Media Production, which conflicts with the Canadian study visa choice and the unresolved orientation question; housing with friends at The Blue Lagoon is a social detail, not a milestone; "Recently" and "milestones" are vague.
- Advice given: do not condense these sentences; replace with verified milestones, named program only after confirmation, and remove the Blue Lagoon sentence.

## Finalizing statement, celebration claims (keywords: finalize, Blue Lagoon, July 31, all applications complete, housing, progress claims)
- Aug 1, 2024: user wants to highlight "completing all applications" and "securing housing with friends at The Blue Lagoon on July 31" in the personal statement.
- Notes do not confirm all applications are complete: visa pending (no outcome recorded), UWI scholarship not submitted per May 10 correction, grant statuses unknown.
- Blue Lagoon location unverified; the event is a social gathering, not housing. Apartment already secured per Aug 1 message (rent $1,100/month, currency unconfirmed).
- Advice given: do not include social events or unconfirmed completion claims. Use only documented milestones with confirmation receipts. Keep housing out unless it affects the plan, and then describe it factually.

## Toronto Caribbean Cultural Association, personal statement (keywords: Toronto Caribbean Cultural Association, TCCA, cultural adaptation, July 29, personal statement, visa)
- User says they joined the Toronto Caribbean Cultural Association on July 29, 2024 and attended a first meeting at 7:00 PM EDT (UTC-4) at Queen St. West. Organization name and membership not verified.
- Conflict: notes show the user is still based in Montserrat with a planned move on August 20, 2024. If the meeting was in person, the trip and dates must be confirmed; if it was virtual, the statement must say so.
- Advice given: mention only verifiable facts (join date, role, attendance, what they did). Avoid claiming "cultural adaptation" before the move. Use a specific moment and action, consistent across all versions and the visa form. Ask for membership confirmation and meeting details before adding to the fact sheet.

## Personal statement versions, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: personal statement, academic, visa, grant, word limit, 1000 words)
- Aug 1, 2024: user wants academic, visa, and grant versions of the personal statement, each under 1,000 words.
- Base draft: about 900 words per Kimberly (May 7, 2024). Draft text not in uploads folder. Ask user to paste it.
- Rule from Matthew (June 5, 2024): tailor framing per audience, keep facts identical across versions, especially the visa version.
- Open items that affect facts: 2021 political project excluded (visa concern, Apr 5); 2022 career gap (brief, factual); documentary 2nd place at Janethaven Film Awards (role and proof unconfirmed); TV-to-digital pivot (undecided); Montserrat background paragraph (text not shared).
- Grant prompt, word limit, and the $7,500 grants (deadline May 25, 2024) not in notes; ask for the requirements before drafting.
- Visa/permit status unknown; avoid claims the visa version can't back up.

## Tanya's October visit and user's flight decision, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: Tanya, October, partner, flight, visa, refundable)
- Aug 1, 2024: user's partner Tanya is visiting Toronto for 10 days in October 2024 and booked her flight on July 30, 2024. Tanya was previously noted as a colleague who helped rehearse a pitch (April 4, 2024); the partner relationship is new information.
- User asked whether to book their own flight now or wait for visa approval. Visa outcome still unknown in notes.
- Guidance given: wait for approval unless the fare is fully refundable; Tanya needs her own entry document (visitor visa or eTA, depending on nationality, verify on IRCC); user's own flight should not be booked for October unless the purpose and dates are confirmed. Currency of fares not confirmed.

## Visa-delay contingency plan, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: contingency, visa delay, refundable flight, $150, Toronto visit, apartment, orientation)
- Aug 1, 2024: user booked a refundable flight to Toronto for $150 extra (currency NOT confirmed; date and purpose described as a "visit" in one message, a move in others; clarify).
- User worried about visa delays and asked for a contingency plan.
- Visa outcome still unknown in notes (interview June 10, 2024). Orientation (September 2, 2024) school and campus still unresolved.
- Plan drafted: branch by visa status (approved / pending / refused). Keep refundable flight until approval; check apartment cancellation terms; ask school about deferral if permit is late; hold a reserve from the $4,000 savings; confirm re-entry rules with IRCC or an adviser if travelling while an application is pending.

## Freelance contract and budget, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: freelance, Caribbean Digital Media, budget, rent, savings, $3,500)
- Aug 1, 2024: user accepted a freelance contract with Caribbean Digital Media, $3,500 over 3 months starting September 1, 2024. Pay schedule (monthly or lump sum) and currency NOT confirmed.
- Budget given by user: rent $1,100/month, utilities $400/month, groceries $250/month (fixed total $1,750/month, $5,250 for 3 months). Savings $4,000 for first 3 months. Currency NOT confirmed for any figure.
- Computed: $4,000 + $3,500 = $7,500 vs $5,250 fixed costs = $2,250 left before relocation ($1,500), flight, tuition, transit, phone, insurance. After relocation: about $750. If freelance pays only at the end of the contract, the first 3 months are short by $1,250 before relocation.
- Gap: arrival August 20, 2024; freelance starts September 1, 2024. Costs from August 20 to September 1 come from savings.
- Risk to verify: whether freelance work for a Caribbean employer performed from Canada is allowed under study-permit conditions; tax obligations in Canada and Jamaica; whether the contract is in a currency that needs conversion.

## Orientation conflict and move checklist, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: orientation, September 2, UWI, Toronto move, checklist, overwhelmed)
- Aug 1, 2024: user says orientation at UWI starts September 2, 2024, and the Toronto flight is August 20, 2024 at 4:15 PM (departure/arrival and airport unconfirmed).
- CONFLICT: UWI is in Jamaica, Barbados, and Trinidad, not Toronto. User earlier said they chose a Canadian study visa over a Jamaican option. Which school and campus starts September 2, 2024 is UNRESOLVED. Orientation time, location, and whether it is in person are unknown.
- Permit status still unknown (June 10, 2024 interview; no outcome recorded). Offer letter status unknown.
- User felt overwhelmed. Advice given: resolve the school/campus question first, then build a checklist in priority order (permit and offer letter, flight and fare rules, orientation details, housing already secured, currency of $1,100 rent and $1,500 relocation budget). No timelines given.

## Flight, visa choice, and pre-departure risk, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: flight, August 20, visa, Canada, Jamaica, UWI scholarship, relocation, $1,500)
- Aug 1, 2024: user booked a direct flight to Toronto on August 20, 2024 at 4:15 PM. Departure or arrival, and departure airport, NOT confirmed. Montserrat is AST (UTC-4); Toronto is EDT (UTC-4) in August, so both have the same offset.
- Visa outcome for the Canada study permit (interview June 10, 2024) still unknown in notes. Booking the flight and apartment before approval is a risk; check cancellation terms and whether the permit is in hand.
- Choice of Canada over Jamaica: the UWI Caribbean Scholarship ($5,000, deadline May 15, 2024) may be tied to a Jamaican program. Status unknown; user had not submitted it per the May 10 correction. Confirm with UWI before assuming the switch is safe.
- Canadian offer letter (DLI acceptance) status not in notes. Needed for the study permit.
- $1,500 relocation budget: currency NOT confirmed (user preference: state currency). Relocation money is not proof of funds for a study permit.
- No August 1, 2024 deadline is recorded in notes. The user cited a "time anchor" pressure; ask what it refers to.
- Advice given: do not count on the flight or apartment before the visa is confirmed; ask airline about fare rules and travel insurance; verify entry requirements on IRCC.

## Toronto apartment and networking, Aug 1 2024 (keywords: Toronto, apartment, Sarah, Matthew, LinkedIn, grant reviewer, UWI)
- Aug 1, 2024: user secured a furnished apartment in Toronto at $1,100/month. Currency NOT confirmed; assumed CAD. Ask before quoting it as a budget figure (user preference: state currency).
- User said the apartment is "near UWI campus". UWI (University of the West Indies) has no Toronto campus. Ask which school or campus they mean before giving location-based advice.
- July 25, 2024: Matthew introduced user via LinkedIn to Sarah, a grant reviewer and colleague of Danielle. This intro is NOT the same context as the June 5 Montserrat Media Hub Matthew entry; assume the same person until confirmed.
- Advice given: request a short informational chat about the grant review process and career path; do not ask Sarah for insider info on pending or specific applications; disclose any relationship with her if she reviews the user's applications.
- Networking ideas for Toronto: university media/film programs, Toronto International Film Festival (September 2024), Hot Docs, Canadian Media Producers Association, Toronto Arts Council (grant body).
- Caveat: networking and any paid work depend on the user's permit status (study-permit work limits). Verify before taking paid roles.
- Open: the Canadian visa decision outcome (interview June 10, 2024) is not in notes; confirm before advising on work or networking limits.

## User preferences (keywords: currency, preferences, budget formatting)
- June 15, 2024: user asked that every financial amount or budget be given with its currency specified. Earlier amounts in this project (e.g., $1,500 relocation, $2,000 emergency fund, $3,200 freelance income, $25/hour job, $300 clothing, $1,200/month) were written with "$" only; currency not confirmed. Ask which currency applies (e.g., XCD, JMD, CAD, USD) before giving any new figure.

## Matthew, Montserrat Media Hub (keywords: Matthew, grant, personal statement tailoring, June 5)
- User met Matthew at Montserrat Media Hub on June 5, 2024. He gave tips on adapting personal statements for grant applications.
- June 15: user plans to contact him again for advice on tailoring the personal statement for global opportunities.
- No prior notes on Matthew's role or advice in memory; ask user for his suggestions before drafting.
- Caution given: tailor framing for each opportunity, but keep the facts identical across all versions, especially the one used for the visa and study application.

## Canada visa interview, June 10 2024 (keywords: visa interview, Kingston, consulate, stress, June 10)
- User had a Canadian visa interview on June 10, 2024 at the Canadian Consulate in Kingston; it lasted 25 minutes.
- On June 15 the user said they were stressed and asked whether they handled stress well enough to make a good impression.
- Assistant could not judge the impression from a summary. Outcome not known as of June 15; decisions can take time.
- Interview is a surprise vs. earlier note that study permits often have no interview; user had likely been asked to attend.
- Next step: user to share what was asked and how they answered if they want specific feedback.

## Deadlines and meetings (keywords: deadline, meeting, Danielle, scholarship, visa, March 2024)
- Personal statement draft: target completion March 31, 2024 (about 40% done as of Mar 15), then two revision rounds.
- Zoom review with Professor Danielle: user stated it was rescheduled to March 22, 2024 at 4:30 PM. Earlier the user said 3 PM. Use the latest, confirm against the Zoom invite. Montserrat is UTC-4 year-round (AST).
- Personal statement finish goal: April 20, 2024.
- UWI Caribbean Scholarship ($5,000) deadline: May 15, 2024.
- May 10, 2024: user worried about the scholarship. Bryan agreed to write a recommendation letter due May 20, 2024, which is five days AFTER the May 15 scholarship deadline. Flag this conflict; confirm whether the scholarship accepts a later letter or whether a different recommender or a letter sent directly is needed.
- May 10, 2024: user worried about a $50 late penalty for the May 15 scholarship deadline and asked how to prioritize final edits. The $50 penalty is not in notes and is unverified. Bryan's letter (due May 20) is the bigger risk, not the statement edits.
- Visa application due: June 1, 2024 (Canada; $150 fee, refundability unverified).
- May 10, 2024: user thanked Wendy for a handwritten letter (May 5) urging them to emphasize resilience in the personal statement. Wendy's role and letter text are not in notes. Advice: show resilience through a specific moment and action, not the label.
- May 10, 2024: user at Montserrat Public Library for about 15 hours and worried about continuing there. Advice given: judge by progress, not hours; stop when a task is done; protect the 7-9 AM window.
- May 10, 2024: user has 3 full drafts and 2 peer reviews, and asked whether the final version is ready for submission by May 12, 2024. Final text, word limit, and portal requirements not yet shared.
- May 10, 2024: user is excited about a part-time producer role at Montserrat Media Hub paying $25/hour, and worried whether it will cover studies. Hours per week, tuition, and living costs not in notes. Flag: work rules on a Canadian study permit may limit or restrict this job; verify with IRCC or an adviser.
- May 10, 2024: user ACCEPTED the part-time Montserrat Media Hub role starting June 1, 2024 (same day as the Canada visa due date). User asked to weigh how this affects choosing Canada over Jamaica. Work-rule implications on a study permit need verification.
- May 10, 2024: user asked what steps to take to prepare for a Canadian visa interview if they choose Canada. Note: Canadian study permits often don't involve an interview; IRCC may request one. Answer truthfully; no coaching to conceal anything.
- May 10, 2024: user worried about workload. Tanya expressed concern on May 6, 2024 (her specific concern not recorded). User asked whether weekly check-ins are enough or whether more frequent meetings are needed.
- CORRECTION (May 10, 2024): an earlier entry said the user uploaded the scholarship application on May 14 at 11:45 PM. That cannot be right, since today is May 10 and the user later said they have never submitted a scholarship application or uploaded documents online. Treat the scholarship application as NOT submitted. Bryan's letter status not confirmed. Award notification process not in notes.
- May 10, 2024: user booked an immigration consultant session on May 20, 2024 for visa interview skills. Worried about Toronto living costs, which user estimates at about $1,200/month excluding rent, and how that affects the application. Advice: IRCC proof-of-funds minimum is higher than that figure (verify current amount); rent is not included; check the consultant is licensed (RCIC or CICC).
- May 10, 2024 (follow-up): user asked how to use the $1,200/month figure to strengthen the visa application. Advice: the figure can't be presented as sufficient; use a documented budget with rent from real listings and the current IRCC minimum; verify source of the $1,200 figure.
- May 10, 2024: user asked whether to include the Montserrat Media Hub job (starts June 1) as income in financial documentation. Advice: proof of funds generally shows existing funds, not future wages; job has not started; don't count it as funds. Offer letter may support the study plan or ties, if accurate. Confirm with consultant on May 20.
- May 10, 2024: user asked whether to state exact planned weekly hours for the Montserrat job. Advice: only if the employer has confirmed the hours in writing; never exceed study-permit work limits; ask consultant on May 20.
- May 10, 2024: user worried Danielle (academic advisor) praised the final draft's voice consistency only to be nice. Advice: specific praise is a real signal; ask her one direct question about the weakest section.
- May 10, 2024: user says their documentary won 2nd place at the Janethaven Film Awards on March 28, 2024, and asked how to use it to boost application credibility. Role on the film, award category, and proof (certificate or listing) not yet confirmed. Advice: state verifiable facts and their own role accurately; attach evidence if the application allows.
- May 10, 2024: user is considering shifting focus from TV production to digital content creation after Shawn's feedback (April 2, 2024). Asked how to communicate the pivot in the personal statement. Not yet decided; the statement is near final, so a pivot would conflict with the TV/documentary material unless reframed. Program focus fit still unconfirmed.
- May 10, 2024: user rewrote the statement conclusion on May 8 to add a call to action about media's role in social change, and asked if it is impactful enough. Conclusion text not shared yet.
- May 10, 2024: user added a paragraph on how their Montserrat background informs a global media perspective, "as per Shawn's feedback," and asked if it will help with global opportunities. Paragraph text not shared; Shawn's feedback still not recorded in notes.
- May 10, 2024: user says they decided on a Canadian study visa instead of a Jamaican option, citing better funding. Asked how to explain this transition in the personal statement. Open questions: whether the UWI scholarship is tied to a Jamaican program, and whether a Canadian offer letter is in hand for the June 1 application.
- Immigration consultant session: May 20, 2024, 2:00 PM AST (UTC-4), per user (May 10, 2024). Toronto is also UTC-4 that day (EDT), so times match. Assistant cannot add to a calendar; user must. Consultant's licence not yet verified.
- Preferred writing window: 7-9 AM.
- Note: I cannot set reminders or calendar alerts; user must do that.

## Date format preference (keywords: date format, deadlines, month-day-year)
- User wants deadline dates written month-day-year (e.g., March 22, 2024) whenever they ask about deadlines.

## Personal statement feedback from Kimberly (keywords: Kimberly, personal statement, transitions, documentary, Janethaven)
- May 7, 2024: met Kimberly at Café Montserrat. She praised the improved flow of the 900-word personal statement. User is unsure whether it is good enough for the grant application. Grant prompt and word limit not yet confirmed in notes.
- May 10, 2024: user worried about meeting a May 25, 2024 deadline for two additional grants totaling or offering $7,500 and asked to tailor the statement to how that funding changes study plans. Grant names, criteria, and the breakdown of the $7,500 are not in notes; ask before drafting.
- Kimberly reviewed the revised draft on April 3, 2024. Main note: weak transitions between academic and personal sections.
- She suggested adding a story about a local documentary that won 2nd place at the Janethaven Film Awards.
- As of Apr 5 the user was stuck on how to fit that story in. No draft text was in the uploads folder, so the draft and her comments were not reviewed.

## Shawn meeting, storytelling insights (keywords: Shawn, Bryan, Media Hub, storytelling insights)
- User met Shawn (81, veteran producer) through Bryan on April 1, 2024 at Montserrat Media Hub; Shawn shared insights on storytelling impact.
- Insights not recorded in session. Ask the user for notes before drafting anything that attributes ideas to Shawn.
- Also noted: university application submission planned for April 25, 2024 (official deadline not confirmed in notes).

## Career pivot idea (keywords: pivot, digital content, TV production, Shawn feedback)
- On April 2, 2024, after feedback from Shawn, user considered pivoting from TV production to digital content creation.
- Open question for the statement: whether the target program's focus matches the new direction. Not yet confirmed.

## Editing budget (keywords: budget, editing, East Janethaven Writers' Studio, $200)
- User has $200 set aside for professional editing at East Janethaven Writers' Studio, session April 15, 2024.
- Studio rates and what $200 covers are unknown (not verified). Ask the studio for a quote and scope before the session.

## Sensitive items raised Apr 5 (keywords: visa, 2021 political project, 2022 career gap)
- User decided to exclude a 2021 political project from the statement, worried about visa issues. Advice given: statement is persuasive, but any form question must be answered accurately; check with university international office or an immigration adviser. No visa-risk prediction made.
- User asked about explaining a 2022 career gap due to family illness. Plan: brief, factual, no medical detail required; keep consistent with the CV and any gap question on forms.

## Mock interview with Danielle (keywords: Danielle, mock interview, April 18, Zoom)
- Mock interview with academic advisor Danielle on April 18, 2024, 10 AM, via Zoom (Montserrat, AST UTC-4).
- User is nervous; Tanya helped rehearse a 5-minute personal pitch on April 4.

## Freelance pause (keywords: freelance, pause, April 6, time management)
- User paused freelance work for 3 weeks starting April 6, 2024. That runs past the April 20 statement target and the April 25 submission date, so the pause ends after both.
- Flagged for user: confirm the pause covers the application window and check whether the end date needs to change.

## Coursera academic writing course (keywords: Coursera, academic writing, April 10)
- User enrolled in a 4-week online academic writing course via Coursera starting April 10, 2024. It runs to about May 7, after the April 20 statement target and the April 25 submission.
- Advice given: use only the lessons that apply to the current statement; don't let the course add a new task before the deadlines.
- May 10, 2024: user asked for help reflecting on Coursera feedback to improve narrative compression without losing impact. The feedback text was not in memory or uploads; asked user to paste it. Submission status of the statement after April 25 is unknown; ask before assuming.

## Editing session moved (keywords: editing, April 18, rescheduled, conflict)
- Professional editing session at East Janethaven Writers' Studio moved from April 15 to April 18, 2024.
- Conflict: April 18 is also the Danielle mock interview (10 AM Zoom). Only 2 days remain before the April 20 statement target to act on edits.

## User preference: exact times for appointments (keywords: appointments, meetings, exact time, times)
- When the user asks about appointments or meetings, always give the exact time (with time zone, Montserrat is AST UTC-4). If the time isn't known, say so and ask for it rather than estimating.

## User preference: name tools (keywords: preference, tool names, writing aids, software)
- When discussing writing aids or software, always include the specific tool names (for example Grammarly Premium, Hemingway Editor, ProWritingAid, LanguageTool, Microsoft Editor).
